cards.title: Belief under audit: limiting frontier AI is what creates a permanent underclass
cards.summary: Reader: the X and tech crowd worried that capping frontier models locks in economic inequality. Payoff: they see the underclass already exists, so the fear is pointed at the wrong target. Technical altitude, maps to X. The observable: look up the current US Gini wealth index yourself, one search, under a day. Carried verbatim by line 13.

cards.title: Belief under audit: meeting a real threat requires granting supernormal powers
cards.summary: Reader: the civic and political audience worried about emergency power consolidation riding in on AI. Payoff: a concrete question to chase instead of a mood, has any society ever answered a genuine threat without handing over supernormal powers. Society and political altitude, maps to Bluesky. The observable: find one historical case in an afternoon of reading. Carried verbatim by lines 15 and 17.

cards.title: Belief under audit: you can only argue about wealth and power, you cannot test the assumptions
cards.summary: Reader: practitioners and builders who hold strong priors about society, wealth, and power. Payoff: they can check those priors against real data now, hand the problem to Claude and its datasets instead of trading vibes. Professional and builder altitude, maps to LinkedIn. The observable: take one belief you hold about wealth or power and ask Claude to check it against the data, under a day. Carried by line 19 and lines 21-23.

cards.title: CTA check: reads as society_capitalism_piece, ai_agency_thesis second, source is the CTA
cards.summary: Per config/content-types.yaml this is a society-level inequality and power reflection (society_capitalism_piece), with the rogue-AI and agency thread also fitting ai_agency_thesis. Both resolve the primary CTA to source, the note's own canonical_url. No project_url is present and none should be guessed. One question for you: on the power-consolidation angle (r1-c2), do you want the voting tool attached as a project CTA (a literal civic-tech override), or keep it source-only. I will not invent a project link.

cards.title: Spin fit: strong on X and Bluesky, LinkedIn falls back to non-case
cards.summary: X (tech): strong, the Gini angle names a real observable rather than a generic AI-is-like-X gloss. Bluesky (political): strong, the power-consolidation and fairness-gap framing is its approved angle. LinkedIn (business and career): partial, the source has no work scene with a number plus a literally quoted belief, so it fails beat 2 of the case template and should fall back to normal extraction, not a forced case. Substack (society) builder-philosopher angle fits the material, but Substack essays are not a routing target here.
